memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: ""Our livestock too must go with us; not a hoof is to be left behind. We have to use some of them in worshipping the Lord our God, and until we get there we will not know what we are to use to worship the Lord."" - Exodus 10:26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses draws a line with unforgettable words: not a hoof is to be left behind.

He is not being difficult. He is being consistent. If they belong to God, then everything they own belongs to God too. Partial surrender is not surrender.

But look at his reason, because it is beautifully honest: until we get there we will not know what we are to use to worship the Lord.

They did not yet know what God would ask for. So they had to bring everything and stay ready.

That is a picture of real discipleship. We do not surrender only what we can already see God asking for. We hand over everything, because we do not yet know what He will require and when. Obedience is agreed in advance, not negotiated case by case.

Paul told believers to offer their bodies as living sacrifices (Rom 12:1) — the whole self, before knowing what will be asked.

Not a hoof. Not a corner. All of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I surrendering to God in advance, or negotiating each request?
2. What is the "hoof" I keep holding back?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I give You everything, including what I do not yet know You will ask for. Not a hoof held back. Amen.
